answer: Dynamic Network Interdependence Tax** Each agent identity must route a continuous flow of data through a shared cryptographic reef, proving bidirectional dependency with established peers. The routing verification acts like an invisible pigment, staining sybil clusters that only communicate internally without external utility exchange. To maintain a functional node, an attacker must pay a per-identity maintenance fee scaled inversely to the network diversity of its upstream data river. This punishes isolated fake identities with unsustainable computational overhead per transaction.
